name: How Much Greenery Do You See? (Helsinki, 0–100)
description:
Method replication: the paper's greenery question and 0–100 scale, asked online about street-level photos instead of on site. Images: 100 Helsinki street-level photos from Mapillary (CC BY-SA 4.0, © Mapillary contributors), a sample released by the first author on Hugging Face (Jusba/Greenery_Survey_Helsinki_Mapillary); they are not the paper's study sites. Torkko, Poom, Willberg & Toivonen (2023, Frontiers in Sustainable Cities 5:1160995) asked people at randomly selected sites across Helsinki how much greenery they saw around them, from 0 (no visible greenery) to 100 (only greenery is visible), and compared the answers with street-level (image segmentation, colour segmentation, point clouds) and top-down (land cover, remote sensing) greenery maps. All methods were strongly associated with perceived greenery, but mapped values were consistently lower than perceived ones; semantic segmentation came closer to human perception than colour segmentation.

What participants do: after consent, 20 Helsinki photos drawn at random from 100; for each they move a slider from 0 to 100 for how much natural greenery they see (ignoring green cars, buildings and other artificial objects). Then familiarity with Helsinki and age.

Analysis as in the paper: mean perceived greenery per image, compared with Green View Index from semantic segmentation of the same image (correlation, and the gap between perceived and measured values).

Differences from the original study: (1) the original was answered in situ at Helsinki study sites; this template asks the same question online about photos; (2) the images are a Mapillary sample from across Helsinki (2015–2025), not the study sites; (3) the familiarity and age questions are additions. The earlier version of this template had an in-situ page opened with ?site= links and no bundled images.
author: Torkko, Poom, Willberg & Toivonen
